st.1: Seals are a distinctive feature of the Megalithic culture of South India.

x: Neither statement is correct. Seals are a distinctive feature of the Indus Valley Civilisation, not the Megalithic culture; the Harappan script is still undeciphered, so seals are a major source on Harappan life.

st.1: Seals were used to stamp and mark goods in trade.

x: All three statements are correct: seals marked goods in trade (they were not coins); a sealing is the clay impression pressed on a package's knot, and an intact sealing showed the goods were untouched and named the sender.

st.2: The humped bull is frequently shown.

x: All three statements are correct: the unicorn is the most common motif, and the humped bull and the rhinoceros are depicted (the cow is not shown).

st.1: Perforated jars were probably used for storing grain.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Perforated jars were probably used for straining liquor, not storing grain; wall paintings are not found at Mohenjodaro.

st.2: Malaria is cited as a problem at Mohenjodaro.

x: All three statements are correct: soil salinity and deforestation, malaria at Mohenjodaro and repeated floods at Chanhudaro are cited as stresses behind the decline.

st.3: He died at Pavapuri at the age of 72.

x: All three statements are correct: Mahavira renounced the world at 30, practised austerities for 12 years, attained Kaivalya at 42 under a sal tree at Jrimbhikagrama, and died at Pavapuri at 72.

st.2: It holds that the universe had a beginning in time.

x: Neither statement is correct. Jainism does not believe in a creator god; it holds that the universe is eternal, without beginning or end.

st.2: The Mahamastakabhisheka of Bahubali is held every 10 years.
st.4: The marble Vimala Vasahi temple at Mount Abu was built by Tejapala in 1031.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The Mahamastakabhisheka is held every 12 years; Bahubali, son of Rishabhadeva, was not a Tirthankara (the second was Ajitanatha); the Vimala Vasahi temple was built by Vimala Shah in 1031 (Tejapala built the later Luna Vasahi).

st.3: The Antapala was the chief of the army.
st.2: The Karmantika was in charge of the treasury.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The Karmantika was in charge of factories and mines (the Sannidhata kept the treasury); the Antapala guarded the frontier forts (the Senapati led the army); the collector-general of revenue was the Samaharta, not the Dandapala.

st.2: It belongs to the first stage of Gupta temple architecture.

x: Neither statement is correct. Bhitargaon is a brick Hindu temple, not a Buddhist chaitya, and it belongs to the third stage of Gupta temple architecture, not the first.

st.2: A kottam (valanadu) was a unit above the nadu.

x: All three statements are correct: kurram was another name for the nadu; the kottam or valanadu stood above the nadu (ur - nadu - kottam - mandalam); a samanta was a defeated king restored as a tributary.

st.2: Ibrahim Lodi wrote under the pen name Gulrukhi.
st.4: Khizr Khan took Delhi and founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1451.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Gulrukhi was the pen name of Sikandar Lodi, not Ibrahim Lodi; Timur left Khizr Khan as governor of Multan, not Lahore; Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414 (1451 is the start of the Lodi dynasty).

st.4: Under the Lodis the Sultan was an absolute ruler who kept the Afghan nobles firmly subordinate.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Muhammad bin Tughlaq brought foreigners and low-born men into high office; under the Lodis the Sultan was only 'first among equals' among the Afghan nobles, not an absolute master over them.

st.2: The second mission came from Diu in 1591.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The second Jesuit mission came from Goa in 1591, not Diu; the third mission (1595), with Jerome Xavier, met Akbar at Lahore, not Agra.

st.1: It had a mass following beyond Akbar's court.
st.3: Todar Mal was its only Hindu member.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Din-i-Ilahi was a small circle of only about 18 members, not a mass following; Abul Fazl, not Badauni, was its chief exponent (Badauni was an orthodox critic); Birbal, not Todar Mal, was its only Hindu member; it ended with Akbar's death.

st.2: Namdev lived in the Tughlaq age, long before Shivaji.

st.2: His Sringara Manjari is regarded as the first Telugu Shringara Satakam.
st.4: He upheld untouchability, as in his song 'Brahmam Okkate'.

st.4: The Indian Universities Act was passed in 1902.

st.2: A district magistrate could demand forfeitable security and seize presses only with the prior permission of the provincial government.
st.4: A paper could obtain exemption by submitting proofs to the High Court.

st.1: Konda Venkatappayya led a 27-member Andhra delegation that met Montagu at Madras to demand an Andhra province.

st.1: Swaraj Party (1923)

st.1: It fought the Marathas in Punjab and then the British.

st.1: It was inspired by Abdul Wahab of Arabia and Mirza Ghulam Ahmad.
st.2: Its Indian founder was Haji Shariatullah of Faridpur.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The movement was inspired by Abdul Wahab and Shah Waliullah, not Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (Ahmadiya); its Indian founder was Syed Ahmad Barelvi of Rae Bareli, not Shariatullah (Faraizi); its followers were mainly peasants and artisans, not zamindars and planters.

st.2: The Eka Movement slipped out of Congress control.

st.3: Madan Mohan Malaviya and Sarojini Naidu attended the Second RTC.

x: All three statements are correct: Gandhi attended only the Second RTC, Maulana Mohammad Ali attended the First, and Malaviya and Sarojini Naidu attended the Second.

st.1: Lord Minto is called the "Father of Communal Electorate".

st.3: Its chairman, Lord William Hunter, had been Solicitor-General for Scotland.

x: All three statements are correct: the Hunter Committee was officially the Disorders Inquiry Committee, announced on 14 October 1919, and its chairman Lord William Hunter had been Solicitor-General for Scotland.

st.3: It was the first movement Gandhi launched on an all-India scale.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The first phase ended with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931), not the Poona Pact; Gandhi's first all-India movements were the Rowlatt Satyagraha and Non-Cooperation, though the CDM was the first to break laws openly on a mass scale.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. The States Department was under Sardar Patel, not Nehru; in the second phase the Kathiawar states were consolidated into Saurashtra, not Madhya Bharat.

st.1: It was constituted at the Nagpur session of the Congress in December 1948.
st.4: It said linguistic provinces should be created at once, wherever they were demanded.

The JVP Committee was constituted at the Jaipur session (December 1948); its members were Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya, not Sanjiva Reddy; it did not favour immediate linguistic provinces, saying only that democrats must submit if public opinion was insistent and overwhelming.

st.1: It was held at Kurnool.

x: Neither statement is correct. The 1936 convention was held at Bellary; it built Coastal-Rayalaseema trust that led to the Sri Bagh Pact (1937), not the Gentlemen's Agreement.

st.3: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was Speaker of the Assembly under NTR's first cabinet.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The TDP was founded on 29 March 1982 when Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy, not T. Anjaiah, was Chief Minister; Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was Deputy Chief Minister in NTR's first cabinet, not Speaker.

st.1: Its microlithic tool centres were discovered by Mortimer Wheeler.
st.2: Andhra microliths are unlike those of the rest of South India.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The microlithic centres were discovered by Robert Bruce Foote, not Wheeler; Andhra microliths resemble those of South India and the Caspian region; the Mesolithic tools of Giddaluru and Khammam are far later than 50,000 BCE.

st.2: The Naga king Nagashoka helped build the stupa at Dharanikota.

x: All three statements are correct: Amaravati (Dhanyakataka) is on the Krishna, the Naga king Nagashoka helped build the stupa at Dharanikota, and its final enlargement was under the Ikshvakus.

st.2: The AP Buddhist circuit links Amaravati, Bavikonda and Sanchi.
st.1: The Buddha is believed to have first taught the Kalachakra at Sarnath.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The Buddha is believed to have first taught the Kalachakra at Dhanyakataka (Amaravati), not Sarnath; the AP circuit links Amaravati, Bavikonda and Thotlakonda (Sanchi is in Madhya Pradesh); the first depiction of Sati belongs to the Ikshvaku phase, not the Satavahana phase.

st.2: The Nandampudi grant was composed by Nannaya, while its donee was Narayana Bhattu.

x: All three statements are correct: Narayana Bhattu came to Vengi as Someshvara I's representative, Nannaya composed the Nandampudi grant whose donee was Narayana Bhattu, and the Korumelli plates share its scribe.

st.2: Bhairavakona, with eight rock-cut Shiva cave temples, lies in the Nallamala hills of Prakasam district.

x: All three statements are correct: Hallisaka (Kolatam) was the popular dance, Bhairavakona with eight rock-cut Shiva caves is in the Nallamala hills of Prakasam district, and the Panchadarla temple has Eastern Chalukya and 15th-century inscriptions.

st.1: Machilipatnam was famous for ratna kambalu (diamond blankets) and carpets.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Ratna kambalu and carpets were Warangal's, not Machilipatnam's; the Palnati Veeracharitra mentions about 1,500, not 500, painters' houses in Orugallu.

st.3: Saluva Narasimha drove the Qutb Shahis out of south-eastern Andhra by about 1470.
st.2: In the Battle of Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya defeated Golconda.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra; at Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya defeated Bijapur, not Golconda; Saluva Narasimha drove out the Gajapatis (the Qutb Shahis arose only in 1518).

st.3: Golconda's old name was Orugallu, and from 1592 the capital was Hyderabad.
st.1: They were Shia Turkmen of the Aq Qoyunlu (White Sheep) tribe from Hamadan.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Qutb Shahis were Qara Qoyunlu (Black Sheep), not Aq Qoyunlu, Turkmen; their court language was Persian, not Telugu; Golconda's old name was Mankal (Orugallu is Warangal).

st.2: Abdur Razzaq, envoy of the Bahmani Sultan, described about 300 ports and the taxation of prostitution in his reign.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Abdur Razzaq was the Persian envoy of Shah Rukh, not of the Bahmani Sultan; Devaraya II's literary hall was the Mutyala Sala, while the Bhuvana Vijayam was Krishnadevaraya's.

st.2: He was the son of Vimaladitya and Kundavai, and married Madhurantaki.
st.4: He built Kulottunga Cholapuram (Machilipatnam) and sent 72 merchants to China.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Kulottunga I was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi (Vimaladitya and Kundavai were Rajaraja Narendra's parents); the Kalingattuparani is by Jayamkondar, not Kambar; Kulottunga Cholapuram was Visakhapatnam, not Machilipatnam.

st.4: Singama Nayaka I was killed in battle by the Gajapatis of Orissa.
st.1: They were also called Musunuri Nayakas.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The Recherla Velamas were called Padmanayakas (the Musunuris were a separate house); the lineage founder was Betala Nayudu, while Singama Nayaka I founded the independent kingdom; Singama was killed by the Jallipalli chiefs, not the Gajapatis.

st.1: It was founded in April 1936 at Faizpur and was first named the All India Kisan Congress.
st.4: Its Kisan manifesto of August 1936 accepted the zamindari system and asked only for lower rents.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The AIKS was founded at Lucknow, not Faizpur; the Palasa session (March 1940) was presided over by Sahajanand, not N.G. Ranga; the August 1936 manifesto demanded zamindari abolition and debt cancellation.

st.4: The Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur, brought out the magazine Natya Kala.
st.1: The first Mahasabha of the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad was held at Rajahmundry in June 1929.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The first Mahasabha was held at Tenali, not Rajahmundry; the Nataka Vidyalayam at Vijayawada was set up in 1964, not 1956; Natya Kala was brought out by the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad.

st.4: Veeranatyam is the dance of Veerabhadra in Vishnu temples.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Chindu are a sub-group of the Madigas, not the Gollas; Veeranatyam is performed in Shiva temples, not Vishnu temples.

st.3: Harikatha is a solo form, in which a single narrator sings and tells the story.

x: All three statements are correct: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu was born at Ajjada, his autobiography is Na Yeruka, and Harikatha is a solo form (the burra-led trio is Burrakatha).

st.1: He was a Shailendra ruler of Kamarupa.

x: Neither statement is correct. Balaputradeva was a Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa, not Kamarupa; his envoy obtained five villages for the Nalanda monastery from Devapala, not Dharmapala.

st.3: Kasu was a gold coin.

x: All three statements are correct: nagarams were market centres, erivirappattanas were protected mercantile towns, and the kasu was a gold coin.

st.1: Its long-term objective is a stable population by 2045.

x: All three statements are correct: the long-term objective is a stable population by 2045, the immediate objective is meeting the unmet need for contraception, and the medium-term objective was TFR 2.1 by 2010.

st.2: Yogendra Singh linked 'empathy' with psychic mobility.
st.4: Milton Singer argued, from Banaras temple culture, that tradition and modernity coexist.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. In Lerner's sequence urbanisation comes before literacy; it was Daniel Lerner, not Yogendra Singh, who linked empathy with psychic mobility; Milton Singer drew on Madras, not Banaras, temple culture.

st.2: The Lokur Committee (1975) tests are primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The criteria for identifying STs are not laid down in the Constitution; the five tests come from the Lokur Committee of 1965, not 1975.

st.1: Periyar was jailed at Guruvayur in 1924.
st.2: Sree Narayana Guru performed the Aruvippuram consecration in 1903.
st.4: Gurram Jashuva was born at Chirala in Prakasam district.

x: None of the statements is correct. Periyar was jailed at Vaikom in 1924 (Guruvayur Satyagraha was 1931); the Aruvippuram consecration was in 1888 (1903 is the SNDP Yogam's founding); the SNDP Yogam is associated with Sree Narayana Guru, not Phule; Jashuva was born at Vinukonda, Guntur district.

st.2: Under the Rayalaseema industrial hub plan, the JSW steel plant is in Kurnool.
st.1: The Ministry of Rural Development monitors 112 Aspirational Districts.

x: None of the statements is correct. NITI Aayog, not the Ministry of Rural Development, monitors the 112 Aspirational Districts; the JSW steel plant is in Kadapa, not Kurnool; Royal Enfield is linked with Tirupati, not Kurnool.

st.1: The UNODC regards India as a source, transit and destination country.

x: All three statements are correct: India is a source, transit and destination country; SITA (1956) was renamed ITPA in 1986; NCRB recorded 696 AHTUs in 2020.

st.3: Assam leads in child marriage cases.

x: All three statements are correct: cruelty by husband or relatives was the largest head, Telangana recorded the most trafficking cases in 2024, and Assam leads in child marriage cases.

st.1: Stunting in India is 19.3%.

x: Neither statement is correct. 19.3% is India's wasting figure, not stunting (about 35.5%); Andhra Pradesh's underweight figure (29.6%) is lower than the national 32.1%.

st.3: The June 2023 protest was over the Maharashtra government's reply to the Bombay High Court.

x: All three statements are correct: NALSA gave an OBC-type vertical quota, the community demands horizontal reservation, and the June 2023 protest was over Maharashtra's reply to the Bombay High Court.

st.1: Antyodaya Anna Yojana gives 35 kg of foodgrain per person a month.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. AAY gives 35 kg per household, not per person, a month; the NFSA maternity benefit is ₹6,000, not ₹5,000.

st.4: Its tagline is 'Kaam Bhi, Daam Bhi'.
st.3: Its Act received assent on 20 December 2025 and came into force on 26 January 2026.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. VB-G RAM G guarantees 125 days, not 150; its Act came into force on 1 July 2026; its tagline is 'Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi'.

st.4: The India-Oman CEPA, in force from 1 June 2026, is India's first CEPA with a GCC country.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The UAE is India's third-largest, not second-largest, trading partner; the India-Oman CEPA is India's second GCC CEPA, after the UAE's.

st.3: The eleventh duty was added by the 44th Amendment, 1978.
st.2: The 42nd Amendment added eleven duties.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The 42nd Amendment added ten duties; the eleventh was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002, not the 44th; the duties are in Part IVA, Article 51A, not Part IV, Article 51.

st.3: The lotus is the national flower and the mango is the national tree.
st.2: 'Satyameva Jayate', from the Katha Upanishad, was adopted as the national motto with the State Emblem on 26 January 1950.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 Chaitra falls on 21 March in a leap year (22 March otherwise); Satyameva Jayate is from the Mundaka Upanishad, not the Katha; the national tree is the banyan (the mango is the national fruit).

st.2: The Dar Commission rejected linguistic States, but the JVP Committee recommended their immediate creation.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Both the Dar Commission and the JVP Committee rejected linguistic States for the time being; Andhra State was created in 1953, not 1956.

st.3: Bammera Potana offered his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu to Lord Rama.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1987 Act regulates temples and mutts in AP, the Hathiramji Mutt is the hereditary Dharmakarta of TTD, and Potana dedicated his Bhagavatamu to Lord Rama rather than to any king.

st.1: The 97th Amendment (2011) added the right to form co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(g).

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The 97th Amendment added co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(c), not 19(1)(g); freedom of conscience is in Article 25, not Article 19(1).

st.2: The 25% quota of entry-level seats in unaided private schools does not apply to minority schools.

x: All three statements are correct: Section 3 gives the right to children of 6-14 years, the 25% quota does not apply to minority schools, and funding is a concurrent responsibility of the Centre and the States.

st.2: The 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles was struck down in Waman Rao (1981).
st.1: Article 31C was inserted by the 24th Amendment, 1971.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Article 31C was inserted by the 25th Amendment, not the 24th; its extension by the 42nd Amendment was struck down in Minerva Mills (1980), not Waman Rao; I.R. Coelho was decided by a nine-judge bench.

st.1: It was inserted by the First Amendment, 1951 in response to Romesh Thappar.
st.2: It overcame the bar of Article 30(2).

x: None of the statements is correct. Article 15(4) responded to Champakam Dorairajan (Romesh Thappar led to changes in Article 19(2)); it overcame the bar of Article 29(2), not 30(2); it covers socially and educationally backward classes too, not only SCs and STs.

st.3: Developing the scientific temper appears both as a Fundamental Duty and as a Directive Principle.
st.1: Article 48A is the citizen's duty on the environment, while Article 51A(g) is a Directive Principle addressed to the State.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Article 48A is the Directive Principle and Article 51A(g) the citizen's duty; protecting public property is a duty under Article 51A(i), not Article 48A; scientific temper appears only as a Fundamental Duty, with no DPSP look-alike.

st.1: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 must be supported by two-thirds of its total membership.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. An Article 249 resolution needs two-thirds of the members present and voting, not of the total membership; a censure motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.

st.3: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, during a resolution for his removal, cannot vote at all, unlike the Speaker.

x: All three statements are correct: the Speaker cannot preside but may vote in the first instance (without a casting vote), while the Chairman, not being a member, cannot vote at all.

st.2: The calling attention motion was introduced in 1954.

x: All three statements are correct: the short-duration discussion dates from 1953, the calling attention motion from 1954, and Zero Hour is not mentioned in the Constitution.

st.3: One-half of its members retire every third year.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. The Legislative Council is a permanent house that cannot be dissolved (Parliament may abolish it); one-third of its members retire every second year.

st.1: The minimum of 60 for the Arunachal Pradesh Assembly is relaxed to 30 under Article 371H.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 170 sets 60-500 members; Arunachal's minimum is relaxed to 30 under Article 371H; Goa and Mizoram, with 40 seats each, are exceptions.

st.3: The procedure for impeaching the President is borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.

x: All three statements are correct: the President is elected by STV by secret ballot (from Ireland), candidates needed 10 proposers and 10 seconders between 1974 and 1997, and impeachment is borrowed from the USA.

st.2: The suspensive veto cannot be applied to Money Bills.

x: All three statements are correct: the absolute veto is usually used on private members' Bills, the suspensive veto cannot be applied to Money Bills, and the power to return applies to Financial Bills of Categories I and II.

st.4: He may withdraw an ordinance only with the President's approval.
st.2: He does not need the President's instructions even when a Bill containing the same provisions would have required the President's previous sanction or reservation.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. A Governor's ordinance does not need the President's approval; he does need the President's instructions where such a Bill would have needed the President's previous sanction or reservation; he may withdraw an ordinance at any time.

st.1: It must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months.

x: All three statements are correct: an Article 356 proclamation must be approved within two months, President's Rule can last at most three years, and it can go beyond one year only with a National Emergency and an EC certificate.

st.1: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of an Indian State (the United Provinces).

x: All three statements are correct: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor (United Provinces), C. Rajagopalachari was the first Governor of West Bengal, and J&K's head of State was the Sadr-e-Riyasat until 1965.

st.3: It has original jurisdiction over service matters of members of the armed forces as well.
st.2: It was set up in 1976, when Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The CAT was set up in 1985 under Rajiv Gandhi (1976 is when the 42nd Amendment added Article 323-A); it does not cover members of the armed forces; it does not hear private-sector disputes.

st.3: Even with these new codes, criminal law remains in the Concurrent List.

x: All three statements are correct: the Ninth Schedule was created by the 1st Amendment, 1951; the BNS, BNSS and BSA came into force on 1 July 2024; criminal law remains in the Concurrent List.

st.1: The Chief Ministers' Conference is presided over by the Prime Minister.

x: All three statements are correct: the Chief Ministers' Conference is presided over by the Prime Minister, the Governors' Conference by the President, and water dispute tribunals are statutory bodies.

st.2: The 2022 delimitation of Jammu and Kashmir was done by a Commission headed by Justice Kuldip Singh.
st.1: Officers on election duty remain under the sole control of their State governments, not the Election Commission.

x: None of the statements is correct. Officers on election duty work under the EC's control, and it can transfer or suspend them; the J&K delimitation (2022) was by the Justice Ranjana Desai Commission; Assam was delimited by the Election Commission itself (August 2023).

st.1: The provisions on the office are in Part V, Chapter IV, Articles 148-151 of the Constitution.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The CAG provisions are in Part V, Chapter V (Chapter IV is the Union Judiciary); a single CAG for Union and State accounts is a unitary, not federal, feature.

st.1: Its Chairperson, members and Member-Secretary are nominated by the Central Government.

x: All three statements are correct: the NCW's Chairperson, members and Member-Secretary are nominated by the Central Government; it is a statutory body under the 1990 Act, constituted on 31 January 1992; the CSWI (1974) had recommended such a commission.

st.2: The NHRC Chairperson is appointed by the President and the SHRC Chairperson by the Governor.

x: All three statements are correct: both Chairpersons are removed by the President; the NHRC Chairperson is appointed by the President and the SHRC Chairperson by the Governor; they resign to the President and the Governor respectively.

st.2: If a State withdraws general consent, the CBI must seek consent case by case, including for probes already pending.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The ED needs no State consent under PMLA and FEMA; withdrawal of general consent does not affect pending CBI probes; the NIA Act, 2008 was challenged by Chhattisgarh in January 2020.

st.1: In the GST Council, the Centre has two-thirds of the votes and all States together one-third.
st.3: The GST compensation cess was discontinued for all goods, including tobacco, from 22 September 2025.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Centre has one-third of the votes and the States two-thirds; decisions need a three-fourths weighted majority, not two-thirds; the compensation cess ended from 22 September 2025 for most goods, not all (tobacco kept it).

st.3: Southern States fear that population-based delimitation would shift seats away from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
st.1: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 750.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The 131st Amendment Bill proposed a ceiling of 850, not 750; it was defeated in the Lok Sabha for want of a special majority and never reached the States; southern States fear seats shifting towards UP, Bihar and Rajasthan, not away from them.

st.1: They were first used at Kalpetta, Kerala, in 1982.

x: Neither statement is correct. EVMs were first used at Parur (North Paravur), Kerala, in 1982, not Kalpetta; Goa, not Gujarat, was the first State to hold its entire Assembly election on EVMs.

st.3: It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for examination.

x: All three statements are correct: the 129th Amendment Bill inserts Article 82A, amends Articles 83 and 172, and was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.

st.1: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj, and the Planning Commission accepted its report in January 1958.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The Balwant Rai Mehta report was accepted by the National Development Council, not the Planning Commission, in January 1958; the 1988 Committee on Policy and Programmes recommended a five-year, not three-year, term.

st.3: The Area Sabha of all voters of a polling-booth area was provided for in the 74th Amendment, 1992.
st.1: Wards Committees must be constituted in every municipality, whatever its population.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Wards Committees are compulsory only in municipalities with three lakh or more people; the Area Sabha was proposed in the Model Nagara Raj Bill, 2008, not the 74th Amendment; the Community Participation Law was a mandatory reform under JNNURM, not AMRUT.

st.4: Its SWAGAT-FI (September 2025) is a single-window framework for domestic retail investors.
st.1: It replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Commission.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. SEBI replaced the Controller of Capital Issues (the MRTP Commission gave way to the CCI); appeals against SEBI lie to the Securities Appellate Tribunal, not the NCLAT; SWAGAT-FI is for trusted FPIs and FVCIs, not retail investors.

st.4: The Narasimham Committee that recommended it was set up in 1993 and reported in 1994.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. IRDAI's headquarters is at Hyderabad, not Mumbai; it was recommended by the Malhotra Committee (1993-94), not the Narasimham Committee.

st.2: It issues currency notes, except the ₹1 note and coins, which are issued by the Government of India.

x: All three statements are correct: the RBI manages foreign exchange under FEMA, issues all notes except the ₹1 note and coins (issued by the Government), and a Public Debt Management Cell was set up to ease its conflict of interest.

st.2: Spandana followed the AI-based Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS).

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The sequence was Meekosam - Spandana (2019) - the AI-based PGRS, so PGRS followed Spandana; Meekosam's February 2015 soft launch was in Krishna and Anantapuram, not Guntur.

st.2: Its 4th Report, 'Ethics in Governance', was submitted in 2007.

x: All three statements are correct: the Second ARC was set up in 2005 and gave 15 reports; its 4th Report on Ethics in Governance came in 2007; its 12th Report is on Citizen Centric Administration.

st.3: Under the Industrial Relations Code 2020, 25% of workers or 250 workers are needed to form a union.
st.1: Contract labour fell from about 40.7% of the manufacturing workforce in 1999 to 20% in 2022-23 (ASI).

x: None of the statements is correct. Contract labour rose from about 20% (1999) to 40.7% (2022-23); such firms had about 31% lower, not higher, productivity; the Code needs 10% of workers or 100 workers to form a union.

st.1: APCOS (2020) recruits outsourced staff and pays them directly, cutting out contractors.

x: All three statements are correct: APCOS pays outsourced staff directly without contractor middlemen, the Civil Services Board curbs political interference in postings, and the age limit was raised from 42 to 44.

st.3: Mizoram was the first State to approve a draft State Water Policy (2019).

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Meghalaya, not Mizoram, was the first State to approve a draft State Water Policy (2019); Tamil Nadu, not Kerala, first made rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all buildings.

st.1: Under Article 262(2) the President may bar the Supreme Court and other courts from such disputes.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Under Article 262(2) it is Parliament, not the President, that may bar the courts; Articles 265 and 268 deal with taxation, not water disputes.

st.3: The NFFWP and SGSY were subsumed into NREGA in its districts from 2006.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The NFFWP was launched in the 150, not 250, most backward districts; NREGA subsumed the NFFWP and SGRY (the SGSY became the NRLM in 2011).

st.3: Bharat Nirman
st.1: Minimum Needs Programme

x: Matching / ordering question, not a statement set: its items are left unchanged and the original key stands (notes_realign.apply keeps such questions as they are).

st.3: Private corporate investment was 11.2% of GDP in FY24.

x: All three statements are correct: MoSPI's NSO estimates saving by institutional sector, household saving fell from 18.6% to 18.1% of GDP, and private corporate investment was 11.2% of GDP in FY24.

st.3: As per PLFS 2023-24, India's rural and urban unemployment rates were 5.1% and 2.5%.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. India's PLFS 2023-24 (UPSS) unemployment rate was 3.2%, not 4.1%; the rural rate was 2.5% and the urban 5.1%, not the other way round.

st.3: It has about 31.89 crore registrations and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.
st.1: It is a national database of organised-sector workers.

x: None of the statements is correct. e-Shram is a database of unorganised, not organised, workers; most gig workers are still outside it; it is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not Rural Development.

st.2: Ex-CEA Arvind Subramanian estimated 2011-17 growth at about 9%, above the official 7%.
st.1: The Finance Commission (June 2026) projected growth of 6.6% for 2026-27.

x: None of the statements is correct. The 6.6% projection for 2026-27 was the RBI's (June 2026), not the Finance Commission's; Subramanian estimated 2011-17 growth at about 4.5%, below the official 7%; in 2025-26 AP grew 9.88% against India's 7.4%.

st.3: It is the first State to bring out quarterly economic reports.
st.4: The Swarna Andhra @2047 vision targets a GSDP of Rs 308 lakh crore (about $24 trillion).

x: Only statement 1 is correct. AP's per capita income (Rs 2,94,507) is above, not below, the national figure (Rs 2,19,575); AP is the first State to bring out monthly, not quarterly, economic reports; Rs 308 lakh crore is about $2.4 trillion, not $24 trillion.

st.2: The Samaveshi Aajeevika Yojana is run by Bihar under its JEEViKA mission.
st.3: Tamil Nadu is moving to extreme-poverty-free status.
st.1: Odisha runs the Satat Jeevikoparjan Yojana, a graduation-approach model.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Satat Jeevikoparjan Yojana is Bihar's, not Odisha's; the Samaveshi Aajeevika Yojana is the Centre's under DAY-NRLM; it is Kerala, not Tamil Nadu, that is moving to extreme-poverty-free status; VB-G RAM G guarantees 125 days, not 150.

st.3: Article 39(c) directs the State to minimise inequalities in income and Article 38(2) to prevent concentration of wealth.
st.1: Wealth tax was abolished in India in 1985.

x: None of the statements is correct. Wealth tax was abolished from 1 April 2016 and estate duty in 1985 (not 1995); Article 38(2) is on minimising income inequalities and Article 39(c) on preventing concentration of wealth.

st.3: India moved towards indicative planning from the Eighth Plan.

x: All three statements are correct: imperative planning replaces the market with a command hierarchy, Stalin's USSR and China are examples, and India moved to indicative planning from the Eighth Plan.

st.3: The Fourth Plan targeted agricultural growth of 5% a year.

x: All three statements are correct: the Third Plan grew only 2.2% against 5.6%, the Fourth Plan achieved 3.3% against 5.7%, and it targeted agricultural growth of 5% a year.

st.3: The shares of all five southern States rose under its formula.

x: All three statements are correct: the 16th Finance Commission kept the States' share at 41%, its award period is 2026-27 to 2030-31, and all five southern States' shares rose.

st.2: Irrigation and power projects were a criterion in the original Gadgil formula but not in the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula.

x: All three statements are correct: the Gadgil formula was used from the Fourth Plan, irrigation and power projects (10%) figured in it but were dropped in the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, and the first Special Category States got 90% grant and 10% loan.

st.2: When the public deposits currency in banks, money supply does not change.

x: All three statements are correct: RBI purchases of securities inject reserve money and raise money supply, while depositing or withdrawing currency only shifts money between currency and deposits, leaving money supply unchanged.

st.1: In FY 2025-26 UPI accounted for about 85% of India's digital payment value.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. UPI's 85% share is of digital payment volume, not value; monthly UPI transactions first crossed 2,000 crore in August 2025, not August 2024.

st.2: Directors of the Central Board hold office for 4 years.

x: All three statements are correct: the RBI's Central Board has 21 members, its directors hold office for 4 years, and the Governor is appointed by the Government for up to 5 years.

st.2: Qualitative instruments are also called selective credit control.

x: All three statements are correct: qualitative instruments regulate the direction of credit and are also called selective credit control, while the bank rate is a quantitative instrument.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh still runs a primary deficit.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's BE 2026-27 shows a revenue deficit of 1.11% and a fiscal deficit of 3.84% of GSDP, and the State still runs a primary deficit.

st.1: Basic customs duty and CVD on imports were subsumed in GST.

x: Neither statement is correct. Service tax and CVD were subsumed in GST, but basic customs duty was not; State excise on alcoholic liquor was also kept outside GST.

st.3: The Special Rupee Vostro Account is an RBI mechanism for settling trade in rupees.

x: All three statements are correct: the Rapid Credit Facility gives concessional support to low-income countries, the SBA and EFF are regular IMF windows, and the SRVA is an RBI mechanism (not an IMF facility) for rupee trade settlement.

st.3: Child stunting and wasting depend also on non-food factors such as sanitation and genetics.

x: All three objections are correctly stated: three of the four GHI indicators concern children, the undernourishment estimate rests on a small poll-type sample, and stunting and wasting reflect non-food factors too (the GHI uses no income-based indicators).

st.1: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, set up in 1960, was India's first agricultural university.
st.2: In 1966, 18,000 tonnes of Philippine wheat seed were imported.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. India's first agricultural university (1960) was G.B. Pant University, Pantnagar, not PAU Ludhiana; the 18,000 tonnes of wheat seed imported in 1966 were Mexican; the Early Green Revolution was 1968-81 (1981-92 is the later phase).

st.3: Consolidation of holdings failed to take off in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

x: All three statements are correct: Operation Barga (1978) recorded sharecroppers through panchayats, and consolidation succeeded in Punjab, Haryana and western UP but failed to take off in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

st.2: Pavala Vaddi for farmers is a Government of India scheme covering crop loans above Rs 1 lakh and up to Rs 3 lakh at 3%.
st.4: India's farm credit in 2024-25 fell short of the target.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Pavala Vaddi is a State (AP) scheme, not a Government of India one; the GoI's Modified Interest Subvention Scheme gives loans up to Rs 3 lakh at 4%, not 7%; farm credit in 2024-25 exceeded the target (about 104%).

st.3: Stree Nidhi (2011) is a credit cooperative federation promoted by the Mandal Samakhyas and the State government.

x: All three statements are correct: DWCRA began in September 1982 with 75:25 cost sharing, SERP (2000) runs the World Bank-aided Velugu, and Stree Nidhi is a credit cooperative federation, not a Regional Rural Bank.

st.2: They are run by an Estate Officer of the Revenue Department, without commission agents.

x: All three statements are correct: Rythu Bazars began in 1999, are run by an Estate Officer with no commission agents, and about 129 were functional in 2025-26.

st.4: Fortified rice supplied through PDS contains iodine, vitamin A and vitamin D.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. PMGKAY has been extended to 31 December 2028, not 2026; fortified rice contains iron, vitamin B12 and folic acid.

st.2: Of the operating CPSEs in 2024-25, 226 were profit-making and 63 loss-making.

x: All three statements are correct: there were 5 CPSEs in 1951 and 291 operating in 2024-25, of which 226 made profits and 63 losses.

st.3: Schedule C industries were left to private initiative, free of any licensing.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Aluminium was in Schedule B, not A; Schedule C industries were left to private initiative but remained subject to licensing.

st.3: After the 2022 reorganisation, Alluri Sitharamaraju and Parvathipuram Manyam replaced Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram.

x: All three statements are correct: NITI Aayog launched the programme in January 2018 for 112 districts; AP's original three were Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and YSR Kadapa; Alluri Sitharamaraju and Parvathipuram Manyam replaced Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram.

st.3: For all States, committed expenditure plus subsidies was 51.76% of capital expenditure (2023-24).

x: Only statement 1 is correct. AP's pensions are about 10%, not 18%, of revenue receipts; the 51.76% figure for all States is of revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure.

st.1: Model bye-laws restrict PACS to credit activities only.
st.2: SIDBI supports PACS as Multi-Service Centres.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Model bye-laws allow PACS more than 25 non-credit activities; NABARD, not SIDBI, supports them as Multi-Service Centres; the CBBO for PACS-FPOs in AP is APCOB, while NCDC gives equity grants.

st.2: Its foundation stone was laid on 26 January 2026.
st.3: It is being built with Reliance Jio and Tata Communications.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The foundation stone of Google's Tarluvada AI hub was laid on 28 April 2026; it is being built with AdaniConneX and Airtel; the APCRDA ecosystem at Amaravati is planned for 9 GW, not 1 GW.

st.1: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was constituted on 24 January 1976 under the Water Act.

x: All three statements are correct: the APPCB was constituted on 24 January 1976 under the Water Act, 'White' industries are practically non-polluting, and EPTRI, Hyderabad, does environment training and research.

st.2: An SME IPO must be listed within T+3 days of the issue closing.

x: All three statements are correct: SME IPOs list on BSE SME and NSE Emerge, within T+3 days of issue closing, and very large firms may now offer only 2.75% to the public.

st.2: India's first weather derivative, RAINMUMBAI, was launched by NCDEX.

x: All three statements are correct: the FMC was merged into SEBI in 2015, RAINMUMBAI was launched by NCDEX, and the F&O market was designed by the L.C. Gupta and J.R. Varma Committees.

st.3: At its closest approach it stays farther from the Earth than Mars ever comes.
st.1: It is the faintest planet visible to the naked eye.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Venus is the brightest planet, not the faintest; at about 41.4 million km it comes nearer the Earth than Mars ever does; it is not the brightest object after the Sun, since the Moon is brighter.

st.2: At 1° interval, 179 parallels of latitude are drawn on the globe.

x: All three statements are correct: latitude is the angular distance north or south of the Equator measured from the Earth's centre; at 1° there are 179 parallels (the poles are points) and 360 meridians.

st.1: Temperature and pressure rise with depth inside the Earth, but density falls.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Temperature, pressure and density all rise with depth; diamonds do rise through kimberlite pipes, but Madhya Pradesh, not Andhra Pradesh, holds about 90% of India's reserves.

st.2: One nautical mile is equal to 1,852 m.

x: All three statements are correct: a fathom is 6 feet, a nautical mile is 1,852 m (1,609 m is the land mile), and echo-sounding depth is speed of sound times half the echo time.

st.3: The Shrieking Sixties blow around 60° S.

x: All three statements are correct: the Roaring Forties blow at 40-50° S, the Furious Fifties at 50-60° S and the Shrieking Sixties around 60° S.

st.4: Polar stratospheric clouds turn reactive chlorine into inactive forms that protect ozone when sunlight returns.
st.2: In 2025 it peaked at just over 21 million sq km and closed unusually late.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The 2025 hole peaked at just over 21 million sq km and closed early, not late; the record of about 29 million sq km was in 2006, not 2015; polar stratospheric clouds turn inactive chlorine into reactive forms that destroy ozone.

st.3: In the 2004 tsunami, the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu was the worst-hit part of India.

x: All three statements are correct: undersea fault movement is the main cause of tsunamis, they travel at over 700 km/h in deep water, and in 2004 the Coromandel coast was hit hardest.

st.3: Their width increases from about 200 km in Kashmir to about 500 km in Arunachal Pradesh.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The Himalaya cover about 5 lakh sq km, not 15 lakh; their width decreases from about 500 km in Kashmir to about 200 km in Arunachal, not the other way round.

st.2: It was reopened for India–China border trade in 2006.

x: All three statements are correct: Nathu La (about 4,310 m) links Gangtok with the Chumbi Valley, it reopened for border trade in 2006, and China halted pilgrims through it during the 2017 Doklam standoff.

st.1: The Kaimur Hills, the western continuation of the Vindhya, extend over MP, UP and Bihar.
st.3: Amarkantak in the Maikal is the source of the Narmada and the Tapi.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Kaimur Hills are the eastern, not western, continuation of the Vindhya; the Maikal is the eastern end of the Satpura, not the Vindhya; Amarkantak is the source of the Narmada and the Son (the Tapi rises at Multai).

st.4: Srikakulam receives the maximum north-east monsoon rainfall.
st.2: The north-east (retreating) monsoon gives about two-thirds of AP's rain.
st.1: The south-west monsoon gives about one-third of AP's rain.

x: None of the statements is correct. The south-west monsoon gives about two-thirds of AP's rain and the north-east monsoon about one-third; by IMD 1989-2018 means September, not July, is the wettest month; Nellore, not Srikakulam, gets the most north-east monsoon rain.

st.3: Afforestation, retaining walls and surface drainage are landslide-mitigation measures.

x: All three statements are correct: embankments, dams and channel improvement mitigate floods; check dams, farm ponds and irrigation mitigate drought; afforestation, retaining walls and drainage mitigate landslides.

st.3: The Mahananda is the last, easternmost left-bank tributary of the Ganga.

x: All three statements are correct: the Damodar joins the Hugli as a right-bank tributary, the Yamuna is the westernmost and longest tributary, and the Mahananda is the last, easternmost left-bank tributary.

st.2: Srisailam is an earthen embankment dam and the source of the Telugu Ganga, Handri-Neeva and Veligonda schemes.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Srisailam is a masonry gravity dam, not an earthen one; the Prakasam Barrage is at Vijayawada, not Rajamahendravaram.

st.1: The Pothireddypadu head regulator is at the start of the Srisailam Left Bank Canal.
st.2: The Telugu Ganga route runs Srisailam – Kandaleru – Somasila – Poondi (Tamil Nadu).

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Pothireddypadu is at the start of the Srisailam Right Main Canal; the route runs Srisailam - Somasila - Kandaleru - Poondi; AP, Maharashtra and Karnataka give 5 tmc ft each (15 tmc ft) for Chennai, not 10 each.

st.3: The card reports pH, EC and organic carbon but no micronutrients.
st.4: Its slogan is 'Har Khet Ko Pani'.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. A Soil Health Card is issued every two years, not three; it reports 12 parameters, including the micronutrients Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn and B; its slogan is 'Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa' ('Har Khet Ko Pani' is PMKSY's).

st.2: Uttar Pradesh had issued the largest number of Soil Health Cards by February 2026.

x: All three statements are correct: zinc, iron, copper, manganese and boron are the micronutrients tested; Uttar Pradesh issued the most cards; most Indian soils lack nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.

st.3: Bamboo and sandalwood come mainly from the mangrove forests of the Godavari delta.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. AP's forest revenue in 2023-24 was about ₹32.81 crore (₹19.63 crore is for 2024-25 to December); bamboo and sandalwood come from the moist hill forests of the northern Eastern Ghats, not the mangroves.

st.1: Moist deciduous forests, the largest forest type of Andhra Pradesh, grow where rainfall is about 75–100 cm.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The largest forest type, growing at 75-100 cm, is dry deciduous, not moist deciduous; short thorn forests grow below about 70 cm, not 50 cm.

st.1: The Congo is the largest continuous rainforest, with the Amazon second.
st.2: The tropical rainforest is the largest terrestrial biome.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Amazon is the largest continuous rainforest, with the Congo second; the taiga, not the tropical rainforest, is the largest terrestrial biome; dense forests lie mostly near the equator.

st.2: Kyanite
st.3: Uranium

x: Matching / ordering question, not a statement set: its items are left unchanged and the original key stands (notes_realign.apply keeps such questions as they are).

st.1: Coal meets about 55% of India's electricity generation.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Coal meets about 55% of India's primary energy needs, while its share of electricity generation is much higher (about three-fourths); India has the fifth, not second, largest coal reserves.

st.2: East Godavari produced 9.64 LMT of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26.
st.1: Departmental tanks in Andhra Pradesh are leased to private aquaculture companies.

x: None of the statements is correct. Departmental tanks are leased to fishermen cooperative societies, not private companies; the 9.64 LMT worth ₹24,345 crore was West Godavari's, not East Godavari's; cobia is a brackish-water, not freshwater, species.

st.1: India's first fertiliser public sector undertaking was set up at Sindri.

x: All three statements are correct: Sindri (1951) was the first public-sector fertiliser plant, the Bengal Iron Works Company set up a steel plant in 1870, and a modern iron unit came up at Porto Novo in 1830.

st.3: Gold is India's largest import item.
st.1: Gems and jewellery were India's top export item in 2024-25.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Petroleum products, not gems and jewellery, were the top export in 2024-25; crude petroleum, not gold, is the largest import; India exports iron ore rather than importing it.

st.4: India's network is the third longest in the world.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Canada (about 49,000 km) ranks below India (about 69,439 route km); India's network is the fourth longest, after the USA, China and Russia.

st.2: India Post Payments Bank was launched on 1 September 2018 under the Department of Financial Services.
st.1: Speed Post was started in August 2006 to compete with couriers.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Speed Post began in August 1986, not 2006; IPPB was launched under the Department of Posts, not the Department of Financial Services; Andhra Pradesh has about 10,660 post offices, not 16,600.

st.2: PLFS 2023-24 put India's literacy (15+) at 80.9%, with a gender gap of 12.6 points.
st.1: The NSS 75th round (2017-18) put India's literacy at 77.7%, with Mizoram top at 96.2%.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. In the NSS 75th round Kerala, not Mizoram, was top at 96.2%; PLFS 2023-24's 80.9% is for ages 7+, not 15+; in PLFS 2023-24 Mizoram, not Kerala, topped.

st.2: Mean years of schooling is measured for adults aged 15 and above.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Mean years of schooling is measured for adults aged 25 and above, not 15; the GNI per capita cap is $75,000, not $1,00,000.

st.2: Agricultural density is the agricultural population divided by the net cultivable area.

x: All three statements are correct: physiological density uses total population over arable area, agricultural density uses agricultural population over cultivable area, and higher natality and immigration raise density.

st.1: India holds about 17.7% of the world's land area (UN WPP 2024).
st.4: The Technical Group on Population Projections projects India's population at 1,522.3 million by 2026.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. India has about 17.7% of the world's population, not its land area (about 2.4%); India overtook China in April 2023, not 2021; the 1,522.3 million projection is for 2036, not 2026.

st.2: Kerala had the highest share of elderly population.

x: All three statements are correct: persons aged 60+ formed about 8.6% of India's population in 2011, with Kerala highest (12.6%) and Jharkhand lowest.

st.1: In Census 2011 the sex ratio was 997 for undivided AP and 993 for residual (13-district) AP.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. In 2011 the sex ratio was 993 for undivided AP and 997 for residual AP, not the other way round; residual AP's sex ratio declined till 1991, not 2001, and improved thereafter.

st.3: The rural and urban Work Participation Rates were 53.3% and 25.5%.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 53.3% and 25.5% are the male and female, not rural and urban, WPRs; main workers formed about 75%, not 60%, of all workers.

st.1: ISRO's 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster is a Hall-type, xenon thruster meant for launch-vehicle boosters.

st.3: LEO imagers give finer detail with periodic revisits, compared with geosynchronous imagers.

st.4: The DDUGJY scheme connected about 26 million households.
